summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis complicated by cirrhosis was admitted with recurrent cholangitis, presenting with fever and right upper quadrant pain. She had recently completed a course of ciprofloxacin but developed symptoms consistent with a flare. Imaging confirmed a persistent 7mm stone in the right intrahepatic duct, which could not be removed due to anatomical constraints. She was treated with intravenous meropenem, transitioned to ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line for a 14-day course, and showed clinical and laboratory improvement. Chronic medications were managed, with lisinopril and furosemide held initially and restarted at discharge. She was discharged home with home health support for IV antibiotics and plans for outpatient MRCP and gastroenterology follow-up.
